source.title: Heavy-light decomposition and long-chain decomposition
source.section: Long-chain decomposition for the k-th ancestor
source.primary_algorithm_description: Lift by the highest power of two not exceeding k, then resolve the remaining upward distance using the long-chain head and offset table.
source.independent_method: Follow parent links for k steps for each query.
source.reuse: Algorithm description only; all ports and fixtures are clean-room.

input.encoding: [N,Q,parent[1..N-1],(vertex,k)*Q]; vertices are numbered in parent-before-child order and vertex 0 is the root
input.parent_rule: For each vertex v with 1 <= v < N, 0 <= parent[v] < v.
input.above_root: A valid query with k greater than the vertex depth emits -1 as its answer.

profile.long_chain_child: Child with greatest height, ties resolved by smaller vertex ID.
profile.query: If k>0, let j=floor(log2(k)); use the 2^j ancestor table entry, then answer the residual distance with the containing long-chain offset or the precomputed ancestors of its chain head.
profile.preprocessing_complexity: O(N log N) time and O(N log N) state.
profile.query_complexity: O(1) after selecting the highest set bit; k is at most 63.
profile.arithmetic: Exact integer indices; all vertices and distances are at most 63.

output.encoding: One vertex ID or -1 above the root, as signed i64, for each query in input order.

workspace.meaning: Six 64x64-bit binary-lifting rows use 3,072 bytes; nine fixed 64-word parent/depth/height/heavy/chain and flattened lookup arrays use 4,608 bytes. Remaining space covers local scalar state, alignment, and ABI bookkeeping; output is caller-owned.
